frontMatter.welcome:
We are excited to have you as part of the JAY FINECHEM PRIVATE LIMITED family. JAY FINECHEM PRIVATE LIMITED is committed to high quality work and superior care in all aspects of our business. As part of the team, we hope you will discover that the pursuit of excellence is a rewarding aspect of your career here.
This Manual is designed to acquaint you with JAY FINECHEM PRIVATE LIMITED and provide you with information about working conditions, employee benefits, and some of the policies affecting your employment. It describes many of your responsibilities as an employee and outlines the programs developed by JAY FINECHEM PRIVATE LIMITED to support you in your job. One of our objectives is to provide a work environment that is conducive to both personal and professional growth. The contents of this Manual are confidential and are not intended for distribution outside of our organization. This Manual remains the property of JAY FINECHEM PRIVATE LIMITED and must be returned upon request.
This Manual and provisions therein may be unilaterally amended, altered, withdrawn or deleted by JAY FINECHEM PRIVATE LIMITED Corporate Office at any time, with or without notice. The HR Department can initiate such revision or change if necessitated by a change in structure, need or responsibilities. Whenever there is change in a policy, JAY FINECHEM PRIVATE LIMITED Corporate Office will update this Manual as soon as possible.
JAY FINECHEM PRIVATE LIMITED HR Policies Manual has the complete version of all relevant Policies and that you can refer to the HR Department for more information / clarifications.
Feel free to discuss with us any questions you may have about this Manual or about your employment at JAY FINECHEM PRIVATE LIMITED.
Sincerely,
Amrut Dama | CEO

Selection Procedure
chapters.text:
- The Selection Committee constituted for that particular recruitment shall carry out all interviews and selection. The Selection Committee shall comprise of following persons for recruitment in each of the grade as designated below:
[table]
| Grade | External Consultants | CEO | General Manager | Department Head Concerned | HR Manager / Executive |
| M3 – M5 | o | * |  | * |
| M1 – M2 |  | o | * |
| E1 – E4, TT |  | o | * |
| S1 – S2 |  | O | * |
| O1 – O4, T |  | O | * |
o - Final Interview Committee and approval
* - Primary Interview Committee
- The selection procedure will have three steps:
- Screening of Resumes: The HR department shall receive all applications. It shall consultatively scrutinize the applications and shortlist candidates whose qualifications and experience are prima facie in conformity with the approved Job Requisition. HR department shall coordinate with the Primary Interview Committee for finalizing the shortlist of candidates to be called for interview.
- Primary Interview Committee: This committee will decide whether an aptitude/ technical test or any other means of evaluating the prospective candidates is required to be administered, for purposes of additional screening, if needed, for general role fit for any particular position.
- HR department shall arrange to send call letters as per the prescribed format to those candidates who have been short-listed by the Primary Interview Committee, stipulating the place, time and date for interview.
- HR Department shall ensure that the candidate fills the Personal Assessment Form as per prescribed format ahead of or on the interview date or before the interview commences.
- Interviews may be conducted at any of the offices of the Company.
- Each member of the Primary Interview Committee shall have a separate Evaluation form as per prescribed format and shall exercise independent judgment for rating the candidate.
- Final Interview Committee: The Final Interview Committee shall interview Candidates short-listed by the Primary Interview Committee.
- Final Interview Committee will recommend the Grade, Annual Emoluments and Other Benefits (viz. Car and Accommodation) to be given to the selected candidate. The recommendation shall be in accordance with the Company’s procedure and policies. Any deviations desired or intended will have be suitably justified, CEO’s specific approval taken before any commitment for a favourable consideration of the same is made to the prospective candidate and the impact of the precedence clearly evaluated and indicated for future policy and practice.
- After selection of the candidate/(s) by Final Interview Committee, HR department will check references provided by the candidate himself / herself before confirming the selection.
- On concurrence of the Final Interview Committee members, HR department shall prepare an approval note and Salary Details Sheet as per prescribed format apprising the Final Interview Committee regarding the qualification, experience, salary offered, total emoluments payable per annum, grade in which he is recommended to be placed. Also, the strengths and weaknesses of the candidates as evaluated during the interview/s and drawn from panel members’ observations shall be comprehensively stated in the form of a note identifying any Competency Gaps and / or any immediate developmental / training needs together with the evaluation sheets. This exercise shall be completed within a maximum period of 15 working days.
- It shall be the responsibility of the HR department that correct advice on the matter of fixation of salary/wages as per the approved grade chart is made available to the committee/(s) to ensure that it does not cause any disharmony in the organization in terms of fitment, salary and designation. The final decision on the salary and other perquisites to be given to the selected candidate shall, however, rest with the Final Selection Committee.
## Reference Verification
- HR Manager, with the knowledge of candidate, will contact references given by candidate through telephone/E-Mail and will get the vital information about the candidate verified. However, this will remain strictly confidential, and it will be done only for supervisors and managers.
- In case, any adverse response is received on reference check, it will be brought to the notice of the Department Head or CEO, as appropriate, and further action will be taken as per his/her direction and guidance.
## Appointment Procedure
- No appointment advice shall be signed and sent until and unless the re-commendatory note is approved by Final Committee Members.
- HR department shall prepare appointment advice as per prescribed format stipulating the proposed date of joining, etc. HR Manager shall sign all the appointment advice and letters. For Grade M3 and above, the CEO shall sign all appointment letters. The HR department will then arrange to send the appointment advice to the selected candidates.

chapters.title: Feedback
chapters.text:
- The new appointee shall undergo the induction process and after completion give his feedback in the form of a report. Copies of all such reports shall also be provided to the CEO’s Assistant.
- The feedback will be analyzed by the HR department and improvements if any in the process shall be implemented.
## Probation / Confirmation
As a new associate, the personnel will go through a probationary period. The length of the probationary period will be specified in the letter of offer for employment and Appointment letter. During this time, the employee will have the opportunity to evaluate the company as a place to work, and the Organization will have an opportunity to evaluate the employee as an associate.
When performance warrants it and at the discretion of the Management, the probation period may be extended.
During the probation there will be performance appraisals at the end of every third month. Probationer will be informed of his areas of improvement in writing. Upon Satisfactory completion of the probation period, HR department will issue a confirmation letter in writing. All associates regardless of classification, status or length of service are expected to meet and maintain company standards for job performance and behaviour.
In case performance is not found satisfactory in spite of time granted for improvement, the services of the probationer will be discontinued. His full and final accounts will be settled along with service certificate within a period of seven days.
PERSONAL RECORDS & PRIVACY
Every employee must submit their documents either on the day of joining or within a week of joining failing which their salary for the month would not be processed. Personnel files are the property of Jay finechem Private Limited and access to the information is restricted.
Employees who wish to review their own file should contact their Department Head or HR personnel with reasonable advance notice, the employee may review his/her personnel file in Company’s office and in the presence of their manager or HR Representative.
Employee records maintained by the company will contain only information that is relevant and necessary to meet various legal requirements and to ensure efficient human resource administration. Please inform the Human Resources Department of changes in personal data and the person to be notified in case of emergency. Up to date records have to be maintained for emergencies and benefit plans.
It is the responsibility of each employee to promptly notify the Human Resources Department of any changes in personnel data such as:
- Mailing address
- Telephone numbers
- Name and number of dependents and
- Individuals to be contacted in the event of an emergency.
An employee’s personnel data should be accurate and current at all times.
- The Company shall ensure that employees receive clear and understandable information regarding the basis of their remuneration and applicable compensation components. This includes basic salary, allowances, incentives, overtime compensation, statutory benefits, deductions and other applicable remuneration components.
- The Company's remuneration framework is designed to provide employees with a clear understanding of how their remuneration is determined and may change over time. Remuneration may include basic salary, applicable allowances, overtime compensation, incentives/bonuses and statutory benefits, as applicable to the employee's role and employment terms.
- Salary levels and adjustments are determined based on applicable job responsibilities, qualifications and experience, internal remuneration structures, individual performance, business considerations and applicable legal requirements. Where applicable, employees may be assigned to defined salary grades, levels or bands corresponding to their roles.
- Salary reviews and advancement may take into consideration performance, changes in responsibilities, promotion, market considerations and other applicable remuneration criteria. Eligibility and calculation of bonuses or incentives, where applicable, shall be communicated to eligible employees through appropriate channels.
- Employees shall have access to appropriate information regarding the remuneration arrangements applicable to their employment and may contact HR for clarification.
- HR shall maintain appropriate records of remuneration-related communications and significant employee queries and responses.
## Adequate Wage
- The Company is committed to providing wages that meet applicable statutory requirements and are adequate in relation to the needs of employees, taking into consideration relevant economic and employment conditions.
- The Company shall periodically assess the adequacy of wages by reviewing:
- applicable statutory minimum wage requirements;
- employee grade and job category;
- normal working hours;
- overtime requirements and compensation;
- applicable statutory benefits;
- relevant industry wage benchmarks;

chapters.title: Promotion
chapters.text:
## Eligibility Criteria
To be considered for promotion, employees must meet the following minimum criteria:
- Tenure: at least 2 years in the current role, unless there is evidence of exceptional performance or business-critical readiness for an accelerated promotion.
- Performance: outstanding performance in the last two performance cycles, measured against clear, pre-defined objectives and feedback.
- Potential: demonstrated leadership potential, cross-functional collaboration, and readiness to handle increased responsibilities.
- Development: completion of key development milestones, including leadership training, participation in cross-functional projects, and acquisition of skills relevant to the next role.
- Performance-centric approach
- Promotions are strictly based on the results of the annual performance evaluation.
- Only employees who demonstrate consistent, measurable achievements are considered.
- No nomination system
- Jay Finechem Private Limited does not follow a nomination or recommendation-based system.
- Promotions are automatically triggered through performance review outcomes.
- Objective criteria for evaluation
- Performance is measured against pre-defined kpis, behavioral competencies, and goal achievements.
- Employees must meet or exceed 90% of yearly goals and maintain a clean disciplinary record.
- Promotion cycle frequency
- Promotions are evaluated annually in q1, following the conclusion of the performance review cycle.
- Exceptional or urgent cases may be considered mid-year with formal business case justification.
- Promotion review panel
- A cross-functional promotion review panel (hr + functional heads) ensures decisions are objective and consistent.
- The panel bases its decision solely on performance data, kpis, and goal achievement—free from personal bias.
- Communication and feedback
- All promotion decisions are formally communicated to employees.
- Those not promoted will receive constructive feedback and a personalized development plan to support future opportunities.
## nternal mobility framework
Jay Finechem Private Limited recognizes that employee growth may occur through various forms of internal movement, not just promotions. Our internal mobility framework supports diverse career paths and learning opportunities:
- Vertical mobility (promotions & advancements): Employees demonstrating high performance and readiness are promoted to higher hierarchical levels, based on:
- Role fit and capability assessment
- Performance history and leadership traits
- Business need and workforce planning
- Horizontal mobility (cross-department moves): Employees can explore different functions (e.g., from sales to procurement) to gain cross-functional experience. This is facilitated through:
- Internal job posting (ijp) mechanism
- Joint manager + hr assessment
- Structured induction and transition plans
- Transversal mobility (cross-skilling roles): Employees are encouraged to move between roles across disciplines when they demonstrate transferable skills. Supported by:
- Participation in cross-skilling programs
- Assignments in cross-functional projects
- Skill mapping and internal talent marketplace tools
## Equal opportunity and transparency:
Jay Finechem Private Limited maintains an unwavering commitment to equal opportunity and inclusive growth:
- All promotion and mobility decisions are made based on merit, competence, and organizational need.
- Hr maintains an internal mobility tracker and promotion dashboard to ensure fairness across departments.
- Employees may express interest in career advancement via the internal career development portal available on the hrms.
## Employee Identification Document Retention Prevention Protocol
At Jay Fine Chem, we are committed to safeguarding the autonomy and privacy of our employees by ensuring they are never required to relinquish their personal identification documents unless absolutely necessary. In cases where it is required for compliance, verification, or other legal purposes, we have established transparent, secure, and employee-focused processes to ensure that no personal identification documents are retained longer than necessary, and that employees have secure alternatives to store their documents.
## No Retention of Personal Identification Documents
Policy on Identification Documents: Employees are not required to submit or relinquish their original personal identification documents (e.g., Aadhaar, PAN, Passport) as a condition of employment or HR processing unless mandated by applicable local laws or regulations.
Clear Communication for Temporary Document Submission: If submission of original documents is required for legal or compliance purposes, employees are notified in writing with:
- Purpose of Submission: The specific reason for requesting original documents, such as statutory verification or government-required compliance checks.

chapters.title: Attendance Policy
chapters.text:
Regular attendance is essential to the company’s efficient operation and is a necessary condition of employment. When employees are unduly absent, schedules and customer commitments fall behind, and other employees assume added workload.
Following are the general shift timings at Jay finechem Private Limited’ locations:
- Mumbai Office: 09:30 AM – 6:30 pm (08.30 Hours)
- Vapi Factory:
- For staff members in the R&D, QA and QC functions, there will be staggered shifts as follows. All R&D members are required to have their lunch at site without exception
- 8 am – 5:30 pm
- 11 am – 8:30 pm
- For staff member in all other departments:
- 9:00 AM – 6:00 AM
- Members must specify to HR beforehand in writing at least 10 days prior regarding their fixed lunch arrangement such that HR can make appropriate settings in the HRMS system. Such changes will be entertained only once every 6 months.
However, hours may vary depending on work location and job responsibilities.
Apart from the general shift, the Vapi factory runs 24/7 and has three working shifts:
- Morning shift 7 am – 3 pm
- Evening shift 3 pm – 11 pm
- Night shift 11 pm – 7 am
Employees working in shifts are expected to arrive at-least 15 minutes before their duty hours to enable smooth handover of duties. Employees finishing a shift are allowed to leave their work station for showering or wrapping up their work day only after their shift timing is over.
Both Mumbai and Vapi administrative offices are closed on Sundays. All other departments in Vapi factory will function on all 7 days of the week. Employees in these departments will be assigned weekly offs by their supervisors. Following guidelines are to be followed:
- Weekly off for staff will be assigned as per consultation with various Department Heads. Department Heads’ weekly off will be assigned by Management.
- No weekly off shall be given on day of shift change and no employee shall remain absent on shift change day.
- The weekly off days will be assigned to workers by their Supervisor or Head of Department. Every employee can avail 4 or 5 weekly offs per month as per their scheduled shift.
- If an employee remains absent on a day other than weekly off, the absence or leave will be considered. If an employee works on his weekly off and takes a leave on some other day, this compensatory off will not be provided without prior approval of HOD or authorized person in writing. Without prior approval, duty on weekly off will be not considered.
- Interchange of weekly off and shift change will be considered only after recommendation of HOD or authorized person. This recommendation must not more than two times in a month and interchange should be in written form.
- If employee remains absent or takes any leave before weekly off/holiday and after weekly off/holiday, the weekly off/holiday will be considered as absent or leave. That means the all three days will be consider as absent or leave.
The Company does not tolerate absenteeism without excuse. Employees who will be late to or absent from work should notify the supervisor in advance, or as soon as practicable in the event of an emergency. Chronic absenteeism may result in disciplinary action.
Employees who need to leave early, for illness or otherwise, should inform a supervisor before departure. Unauthorized departures may result in disciplinary action.
- All workers working on a shift basis receive a 30-minutes meal break around mid-shift and other tea breaks as per norms. The supervisor will assign break times according to department and company schedules.
- Staff employees having lunch on site receive a 30-minutes lunch break at around 1 pm
- Staff employees having lunch outside the premises receive a 60-minutes lunch break at around 12:30 pm
Extra breaks for smoking, snacks, or phone calls are not allowed. Anyone found to be taking unauthorized breaks inside or outside the office/ factory premises will receive a written warning on the first offense.
## Clock in – Clock Out
All employees are expected to Punch in and Punch out when entering and exiting the company premises, both at the Vapi factory and at Mumbai office. Workers are not allowed to leave the factory premises mid-shift. Exceptions will be made only under emergency circumstances and after approval of Supervisor.
Staff employees in the cadre M2 and below are allowed outside factory premises only for lunch and are expected to Punch out and in during exit/ re-entry. If they leave the premises for Company purposes, they will be asked to obtain a gate pass at Security.
Barring emergencies, no employee is allowed to leave mid-shift between 6 pm and 8 am.

chapters.title: Flexible Work Arrangements (For Staff Roles Only)
chapters.text:
To support work-life balance and increase productivity, Jay Finechem Private Limited allows certain flexible work arrangements for eligible staff employees in administrative and non-shift roles, subject to operational feasibility and approval.
The following flexible work arrangements may be considered:
- Staggered Start and End Times: Eligible staff may request to begin and end their workday within a flexible window (e.g., between 8:30 am – 5:00 pm or 10:30 am – 7:00 pm) based on role requirements. Core working hours between 11:00 am and 4:00 pm must be maintained for availability.
- Occasional Remote Work: Staff employees may work from home for a maximum of 2 days per month with prior written approval from their Department Head. This option is not applicable to roles requiring physical presence at the site or factory.
- Split Shifts (Limited Use): On a case-by-case basis, staff may be allowed to split their shift hours in two blocks in a day with an extended break in between (e.g., 8:00 am–12:30 pm and 3:00 pm–7:00 pm) depending on business need and managerial approval.
- Compressed Work Week (Pilot Basis): With approval, staff may work longer hours over fewer days (e.g., 4.5 days instead of 5) such that total weekly hours remain unchanged. This will be implemented on a pilot basis with monthly evaluation.
- Temporary Flex Arrangements: In case of health or personal constraints, employees may request short-term flexible schedules for a maximum duration of 4 weeks. Such requests should be supported by valid documentation and are subject to managerial discretion.
## General Guidelines:
- All flexible work arrangements require prior written approval of the Department Head and intimation to HR.
- Flexibility is not a right and will be granted only if it does not affect team coordination, project delivery, or customer commitments.
- Employees availing flexible work must continue to comply with timekeeping and attendance policies, and be reachable during work hours.
- Misuse or consistent underperformance may lead to revocation of flexible work privileges.
- Department Heads must submit monthly records of flexible work arrangements to HR for monitoring and compliance.
## Shift Change / Rotation
Shift Change / Rotation happens every Tuesday. For example, a worker in the 7 am – 3 pm shift will now work from 3 pm – 11 pm in the upcoming week.
Supervisors will provide employees with their work schedule. Should an employee have any questions regarding his/her work schedule, the employee should contact the supervisor.
Any workmen desirous of changing his shift may interchange his shift other workmen with mutual consent only after written approval of the Department Head. Concerned workmen / employee will make application for shift change at least two days in advance. Additionally, Head of department can also change the shift for administrative reason after due notification to the workmen concerned.
All the departments shift schedule to be shared to HR Department by the concerned department Head before two days of the shift change weekly.
## Late Coming and Early Going
All employees working in shift are expected to arrive at least 15 minutes prior to the shift change time and depart at least 15 minutes after the shift change time to ensure proper handover. For example, the worker/employee is expected to punch in before 6:45am if the shift starts at 7:00am. Similarly, the punch out time has to be after 3:15 pm, if the shift ends at 3:00 pm. Any worker/employee found abandoning their position/duty in the plant before the shift ends will be subject to disciplinary action.
All employees working in the general shift are expected to arrive at the gate at least 10 minutes prior to the shift starting time. This will enable them to be present at their workstations at the shift starting time.
All employees are expected to arrive on time and ready for work. The company recognizes that situations arise which hinder punctuality. Hence, it provides up to 3 grace periods of 15 minutes each within a calendar month. Such tardiness, however, will have to be justified to the Department Head. If an employee exceeds the grace periods within a calendar month, following action(s) can be taken:
- For a staff employee, each “tardy” after the grace periods are used up will result in deduction of ½ day’s Casual Leave. If all Casual Leaves are used up, the tardy will be considered as ½ Leave Without Pay.
- For a worker, he/she is not allowed to resume work without meeting the Manager concerned for counselling. At the discretion of the Manager, any of the following actions can be taken if the worker has used up all the grace periods:
- Each “tardy” after the grace periods are used up will result in deduction of ½ day’s Salary, i.e. the tardy will be considered as ½ Leave Without Pay.
- The Supervisor / Manager / Department Head may ask the employee to return home and the attendance will be marked as a full Leave Without Pay.

chapters.title: Overtime Policy
chapters.text:
Overtime is a condition of employment that may be required in situations where additional work hours are necessary to meet operational requirements or unforeseen circumstances. Employees may be required to work beyond their standard shift hours, provided this is authorized by the department head in advance.
- All overtime work must be approved by the Department Head in writing, either in advance or as soon as practical in case of emergencies. Unauthorized overtime will not be compensated.
- Employees eligible for overtime will be compensated as per the applicable labor laws. The overtime pay rate will be calculated at 1.5 times the standard hourly wage for hours worked beyond the regular shift.
- Overtime is generally applicable for hours worked beyond the normal working hours of an employee’s assigned shift. For example, if an employee works beyond the 8-hour shift, the additional hours will be treated as overtime and compensated accordingly.
- In accordance with the Factories Act, 1948 (Section 59), overtime work cannot exceed 50 hours per quarter (or approximately 2 hours per day). To ensure employee health and well-being, the company limits overtime to 12 hours per month. Exceptions can be made only with prior written approval from the HR and Department Head.
- In lieu of overtime pay, employees may request compensatory time off (compensatory offs) in accordance with the Compensatory Off Policy (refer to Section 2.5.6).
- In cases of operational urgency or critical deadlines, employees may be required to work overtime. Non-compliance with a mandatory overtime request could result in disciplinary action.
- Overtime worked will be tracked through the company's timekeeping system. It is the responsibility of employees to log overtime hours accurately, and supervisors are expected to verify and approve overtime hours worked.
- While overtime may be required, the company is committed to ensuring that employees do not face undue stress or fatigue. Regular monitoring of working hours will help identify potential burnout risks. Employees who are working excessive overtime will be advised to take necessary breaks or time off to maintain their well-being.
- Employees working overtime are entitled to a 30-minute break for every 1.5 hours worked continuously beyond their regular shift.
Disciplinary Action: Failure to comply with overtime authorization policies or reporting overtime hours may result in disciplinary action. The company also reserves the right to review and deny excessive overtime requests that are not in line with operational needs.

chapters.title: Wages
chapters.text:
The company is committed to fair and transparent compensation practices that are aligned with applicable laws, employee roles, and industry standards. The company ensures that all employees and workmen are paid accurately, on time, and in a manner that reflects their role, performance, and statutory entitlements.
- Basic Salary: The core fixed portion of the salary.
- House Rent Allowance (HRA): Aiding in housing costs, based on location and grade.
- Conveyance Allowance: To cover commuting expenses.
- Medical and Special Allowances: For health-related expenses and role-specific allowances.
- Incentives and Performance Bonus: Performance-based variable pay, where applicable.
- Statutory Deductions: Provident Fund (PF), Employee State Insurance (ESI), Professional Tax (PT), Income Tax (TDS), and others as per prevailing laws.
## Wage Policy and Compliance
- Wages are paid in accordance with applicable laws such as the Payment of Wages Act, Minimum Wages Act, and relevant statutory regulations.
- No employee shall be paid less than the minimum wage as notified by the respective government authorities from time to time.
- The company reviews and revises salary structures periodically based on role evaluations, performance appraisals, and market benchmarks.
## Payment of Wages
- Salaries and wages are disbursed monthly, on or before the 7th of each month for the preceding month.
- All payments are made directly to the employees’ registered bank accounts via electronic bank transfer (NEFT/RTGS/IMPS).
- Payslips are generated and shared electronically with employees for their reference and record.
## Overtime and Holiday Pay
- Employees who are required to work beyond the normal working hours or on public/festival holidays are entitled to overtime compensation as per statutory requirements and company policy.
- Overtime wages shall be calculated at twice the ordinary rate of wages, wherever applicable under law.
## Deductions
- Any deductions from salary shall only be made in accordance with applicable laws and after due communication to the concerned employee. These may include:
- Statutory deductions (PF, ESI, TDS, etc.)
- Deductions for leave without pay
- Any approved deductions for loans or advances taken from the company
## Salary Advances and Loans
- Employees may apply for salary advances or personal loans in case of genuine financial emergencies.
- Such requests are subject to eligibility, management approval, and agreed repayment terms, which will be deducted from future salaries in installments.
## Final Settlement
- In the event of resignation, termination, or retirement, the company will initiate the final settlement process, including:
- Payment of earned salary till the last working day
- Encashment of eligible Privilege Leave (PL) balance
- Deduction of any pending dues
- Issuance of full and final settlement within 30 days from the last working day
## Salary Communication and Transparency
The Company ensures that all employees are well-informed about their salary structure, earnings, deductions, and payment timelines. The company follows transparent and consistent methods to keep employees updated about their wages.
## Modes of Salary Communication
- Appointment Letter / Offer Letter: Each employee is provided with a detailed salary breakup at the time of joining through the appointment letter or offer letter.
- Monthly Payslip: A digital payslip is generated every month and sent to the employee's registered email ID. The payslip includes:
- Basic and gross earnings
- All applicable deductions
- Net payable salary
- Bank account details and payment date
- Employee Self-Service (ESS) Portal (if applicable): Employees can log in to the company’s ESS portal (or HRMS platform) to:
- View their current and past salary slips
- Access tax deduction information
- Download income and PF statements
- Salary Revision Letters: Any changes to salary due to promotion, appraisal, or structural revision are communicated formally via email or a printed letter, duly signed by authorized HR personnel.
- Grievance Redressal on Salary: Any employee who has a concern or discrepancy regarding salary can raise it with the HR department via email or the designated helpdesk. All concerns are addressed within a defined turnaround time.
- One-on-One HR Meetings (on request): Employees may request a one-on-one discussion with HR to clarify their salary components, deductions, or taxation queries.
The company is committed to ensuring fair and equitable remuneration for all employees, in compliance with local laws and wage regulations. We are dedicated to creating a transparent and inclusive workplace where
compensation is aligned with the principles of equality, non-discrimination, and fairness, regardless of gender, age, ethnicity, disability, or any other non-performance-related factors.
## Monitoring and Auditing of Remuneration Practices

chapters.title: Maternity Leave:
chapters.text:
Maternity Leave is governed by the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 and Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017. The Company provides Maternity Leave per rules framed there under in force from time to time. Other guidelines are as under:
- Unused maternity leave is not adjusted against the privilege leave balance of the employee or any other leave.
- The Employee will receive the full amount of salary during the period of maternity leave; this will be salary last drawn by the Employee before going on Maternity Leave.
- If the employee wants to extend the duration of leave beyond the stipulated duration, the employee may extend the leave by utilizing her entitled privilege leave with prior permission of the concerned Department / Manager.
- Female Employees who are not covered under ESIC Scheme shall be given Maternity Leave Benefit of 26 weeks with full pay excluding weekly off, which is as per the Maternity Benefit Act 1961.
- This benefit could be availed by women for a period extending up to 08 weeks before the expected delivery date and remaining 18 weeks can be availed post child birth.
- The upper limit for additional leave "Paid" or "Unpaid" is maximum three months apart from Maternity Leave. This is on account of medical problems subject to submission of Medical Documents either before or after Delivery.
- Leave for miscarriage or medical termination of pregnancy, a woman shall, on production of such proof as may be prescribed, be entitled for the period of 06 weeks immediately following the day of her miscarriage or medical termination of pregnancy.
- Female Employees who are covered under ESIC Scheme should register their card with ESIC Panel Doctor. They will be eligible for benefit as per ESIC Scheme. The Employee is responsible to get Permanent ESIC Card
## Leave Without Pay
- Without pay leave is granted only in exceptional circumstances approved by the Department Head and only after all annual leave entitlements have been used up.
- Leave is calculated in full-day unit from the first day of absence until the day of return to work (Week-ends and national holidays are included in the calculation of number of days absent).
- Leave without pay will impact gross salary, i.e. Basic Salary and all CTC components.
## Leave Policy - Workers
This policy is applicable at the Vapi manufacturing to all employees in O1 – O4 and S1 – S2 grades.
## Earned Leave
- Earned Leave as per Factories Act 1948 will be given.
- Earned leave will be given to those employees who have completed 240 days or more in the previous year. If any employee joins in the middle of the year and has not completed 240 days in the previous year he / she should have reported for 2/3rd of the working days, then an employee will be eligible for earned leave. For every 20 days worked in the previous year, he / she will be eligible for one day paid leave.
- The employees should intimate the leave well in advance (at least 15 days prior taking leave) and get it sanctioned on the Leave Form from the HoD and the same has to be submitted to the HR Department.
- In case Leave is taken on emergency basis, HR must be intimated immediately and approval must be taken in writing within 8 days after return from leave.
- Following cases can be subject to disciplinary action leading up to termination:
- Taking Leave without intimation
- Overstay on leave without intimation
- Overstay on leave greater than 8 days without valid, substantiated reason
- Balance of leave, if any, at the end of the year will be encashed at the prevailing Gross Salary.
- Earned leave will always be granted on the basis of leave accrued. No advance Earned Leave will be granted. Leave taken in excess of what is actually earned shall be treated as leave without pay.
- Earned Leave cannot be availed more than 3 times in a year.
- The maximum unit of availing PL would be 30 days at one point of time, including Saturday/Sundays/Paid Holidays. In excess of this, the Leave has to be sanctioned by the General Manager.
- In case of Resignation / Termination / Superannuation the balance leave, if any, will be reimbursed on Pro rata basis.
## Casual Leave
- Workers are entitled to 9 days of casual leave in a calendar year.
- Casual Leave shall be calculated from the date of joining and in case of resignation / retirement and termination till the date of leaving the company.
- The Company does not have provisions for availing Casual Leaves for Workers. However, the accrued leave will be encashed at the end of the year. Casual leave cannot be carried forward or accumulated.

chapters.title: Performance Management:
chapters.text:
Performance management is a shared understanding about how individuals contribute to an organization's goals. An effective performance management and appraisals process focuses on aligning employee’s workforce, building competencies, improving employee performance and development, and driving better towards strategic goals of the organization.
## Goals and Targets:
- Company, based on budget will estimate market conditions and purchase orders will set its goals and split them into quarterly targets.
- Based on Company’s goals and targets, each department’s goals and targets will be set.
- Based upon, Department’s targets, each employee’s goals and targets will be set.
- The process of goals and targets setting will be over by mid of April every year.
- Individual goals targets settings will be in form No. ____ .
## Administration of Appraisal:
A performance appraisal is a systematic, general and periodic process that assesses an employee's effectiveness and productivity and serves both administrative and developmental purposes.
Offer HR support to supervisors.
## Self Appraisal:
Self-appraisal is to be honest and provide as much detail as your manager needs to understand why you've given yourself the rating you have. So be thoughtful about your performance.
Being a good self - evaluator is as critical as being an excellent performer. Being able to put your achievements and growth into words will impact what management thinks.
Self-appraisal also helps you focus on your behaviour. For a meaningful discussion with your boss, it is necessary that you have a great self-appraisal.
The self-evaluation process is your chance to flaunt all that you did well, things that didn’t work out but you learnt from them and other meaningful things.
You can have a number of reasons for not completing your self-appraisal efficiently. The reasons could be lack of time. Feeling that the information is incomplete or sheer laziness. But, this is one of the post crucial part of you evaluation process, so you make time for the same.
HOD / Supervisors are required to evaluate their eligible employees' performance on an annual basis. Employees represented by a collective bargaining agreement will have their performance evaluated according to the terms outlined in the contract. Performance appraisals are conducted on an annual focal cycle.
## Career Development Plan:
- Based on the outcomes of the performance appraisal, a Career Development Plan (CDP) will be created jointly by the employee and their supervisor to outline growth pathways and upskilling needs.
- The CDP will focus on enhancing the employee's strengths, addressing skill gaps, and aligning personal aspirations with the department’s and company's future needs.
- Training, certifications, mentorship, and project assignments will be identified as part of the plan to support employee development over the next appraisal cycle.
- The CDP will be recorded in Form No. 78 and reviewed bi-annually to assess progress and recommend adjustments if required.
- Employees are encouraged to proactively suggest development goals and learning opportunities, which supervisors will evaluate and integrate into the CDP if feasible.
- HR will maintain a record of all CDPs and facilitate access to learning resources and development programs required under the plan.
- The success of the CDP will be measured during the next appraisal cycle, contributing to future performance evaluations and succession planning.
## Equal Opportunity and in Career Development
Jay Finechem Private Limited is committed to providing equal and fair opportunities for career development, professional growth and advancement to all employees. Career development decisions shall be based on objective and job-related criteria, including qualifications, skills, competencies, performance, experience, identified development needs and organizational requirements.
The Company shall ensure that employees are not disadvantaged in access to professional development, training, promotion or career advancement on the basis of gender, age, disability, race, religion, nationality, marital status or any other characteristic protected under applicable law.
## The Company shall ensure the following:
## Equal Access to Development Opportunities
- Employees shall have equal access to applicable training, certifications, mentoring, coaching and skill-development programmes.
- Development opportunities shall be provided based on job requirements, employee competencies, performance and identified development needs.
## Fair Promotion and Advancement
- Promotion and advancement decisions shall be based on documented and objective criteria.
- Criteria may include performance, qualifications, experience, competencies, leadership capabilities, role requirements and organizational needs.
- Personal characteristics unrelated to job performance shall not influence promotion decisions.

chapters.title: Company Property
chapters.text:
Company property, such as equipment, vehicles, telephones, computers, and software are not for private use. These devices are to be used strictly for company business, and are not permitted off grounds unless authorized. Company property must be used in the manner for which it was intended. Upon termination, employees are required to surrender any company property they possess.
Company computers, internet and emails are a privileged resource, and must be used only to complete essential job-related functions. Employees are not permitted to download any “pirated” software, files or programs and must receive permission from a supervisor before installing any new software on a company computer. Files or programs stored on company computers may not be copied for personal use.
Phones are provided for business use. The company requests that employees not receive personal calls while on duty. If urgent, please keep personal calls to a minimum and conversations brief.
Employees are reminded that they should have no expectation of privacy in their use of
company computers or other electronic equipment.
All the company Assets should be tagged as per code according to there name so that the company Assets could be counted and properly maintained.
## nternet & Email Policy:
Jay finechem Private Limited provides job related Internet and e-mail access to its employees in an attempt to improve business communication and productivity as well as give employees’ access to the vast amount of business-related information contained on the Internet. These services are intended to be used solely for business purposes. Every employee has a responsibility to maintain and enhance the Company's public image and to use the Company e-mail system and Internet access in a productive manner. To ensure that all employees act in a professional and responsible manner, the Company has established the following guidelines for using e-mail and the Internet.
Unacceptable Uses of the Internet and Company E-mail:
The Company’s e-mail system and Internet access may not be used for any non-business related purpose without prior authorization. In no event will an employee be allowed to transmit, retrieve or store any information which may violate applicable copyright laws or which may be considered defamatory, discriminatory or harassing in nature. Accordingly, employees are strictly prohibited from using the Company’s e-mail system or Internet access for any of the following purposes:
- Viewing, transmitting, retrieving or storing material that may in any way be considered obscene.
- Transmitting any messages containing derogatory, harassing or inflammatory remarks about an individual or group's race, color, religion, national origin, age, disability, or other characteristic or attribute not related to their job performance.
- Transmitting any abusive, profane or offensive language.
- Transmitting any information which the employee knows or has reason to believe may be false, misleading or libelous.
- Sending or posting any chain letters, jokes, solicitations, or advertisements not directly related to some business purpose or activity.
- Using the Company’s e-mail system or Internet access for any political or religious causes or activities.
- Using the Company’s e-mail system or Internet access for personal gain, including the solicitation of, or engagement in, any non-company business.
- Using the Company’s e-mail system or Internet access for any other purpose which is illegal, may damage the Company’s reputation or is otherwise contrary to the Company's best interest.
- Since the Company has a limited amount of bandwidth to the internet, streaming content such as radio channels and video channels is prohibited.
- Always send documents as .pdf to avoid sensitive data in hidden columns or attachments from being received by the supplier, customer, competitors etc. Further, employees are prohibited from transmitting or posting any confidential material, financial information, trade secret or other proprietary information outside the organization without the prior authorization of their supervisor.
Communications:
Each employee is responsible for the content of all data, text, audio or images that they place on, forward, or send over the Internet or the Company's e-mail system. Employees are prohibited from sending any e-mail or other electronic communication that attempts to hide his or her identity or misrepresent the sender as someone else. All information transmitted on the Company's e-mail system or Internet access must contain the employee's name and other identifying information.

chapters.title: Confidentiality
chapters.text:
The Company shall take appropriate measures to maintain confidentiality throughout the grievance process and protect the privacy and identity of individuals involved.
Information relating to a grievance shall be shared only with persons who have a legitimate need to know for the purpose of receiving, assessing, investigating, resolving or monitoring the grievance.
Confidentiality shall be maintained subject to applicable legal, regulatory and reporting requirements.
## STEPS OF THE GRIEVANCE PROCEDURE
## nitial Reporting
An employee or worker with a grievance should, where appropriate and safe to do so, initially raise the concern verbally or in writing with the immediate supervisor or person responsible for the employee's work.
The grievance should preferably be raised as soon as reasonably practicable after the event or concern arises.
Where the grievance concerns the immediate supervisor, involves serious misconduct, or the employee does not feel comfortable reporting to the supervisor, the employee may directly approach HR, the Department Head, Grievance Redressal Committee or another designated reporting channel.
The receiving person shall listen to the concern, seek relevant information and attempt to resolve straightforward matters promptly where appropriate.
No employee shall be required to confront the person against whom the grievance has been raised.
## Review and Initial Resolution
Where the grievance cannot be resolved at the initial stage, the matter shall be referred to the appropriate Department Head, HR representative or other designated person.
The responsible person may seek advice from relevant management personnel or other competent persons, while maintaining appropriate confidentiality.
The employee may be accompanied or supported by a Union representative, employee representative or other designated support person, where applicable.
Where a grievance affects two or more employees, the Company may request that a reasonable number of representatives communicate the matter on behalf of the affected employees.
The grievance and relevant circumstances shall be appropriately recorded where formal action is required.
The Company shall seek to resolve the matter within a reasonable timeframe based on its nature and complexity.
## Formal Grievance
Where the grievance remains unresolved or requires formal investigation, the employee may be requested to complete a formal grievance form or provide the grievance in writing.
The formal grievance should, where possible, include:
- Nature of the grievance;
- Date and location of the incident or concern;
- Persons involved;
- Relevant facts and circumstances;
- Supporting documents or evidence, where available; and
- The resolution or remedy sought, where applicable.
The formal grievance shall be submitted to the Head of Department, Human Resources Department, Grievance Redressal Committee or another designated authority, as appropriate.
HR or the designated responsible person shall acknowledge receipt of the formal grievance and determine the appropriate course of action.
## Investigation and Hearing
The responsible authority shall conduct or arrange an appropriate investigation based on the nature and severity of the grievance.
The investigation may include:
- Reviewing relevant documents and records;
- Interviewing the complainant;
- Providing the respondent with an opportunity to respond;
- Interviewing relevant witnesses;
- Reviewing available evidence; and
- Consulting appropriate subject-matter experts where required.
All parties shall be given a reasonable opportunity to provide relevant information.
The investigation shall be conducted objectively, fairly and without unnecessary delay.
Where practicable, a person who has a conflict of interest, is directly involved in the matter or is the subject of the grievance shall not investigate or decide the grievance.
For serious or complex matters, the Company may designate an appropriately senior or independent person or committee to conduct or oversee the investigation.
A grievance hearing may be arranged where considered necessary to establish the facts and determine an appropriate resolution.
## Resolution and Remedial Action
Following the investigation, the responsible authority shall determine the appropriate outcome based on the facts and evidence available.
Where a grievance is substantiated, the Company shall take appropriate corrective, preventive and/or remedial action based on the nature and severity of the matter.
Such action may include, as appropriate:
- Corrective action;
- Preventive measures;
- Workplace improvements;
- Policy or process changes;
- Training or awareness measures;
- Appropriate disciplinary action in accordance with Company procedures; or
- Other appropriate forms of remedy.
Where appropriate and subject to confidentiality and privacy requirements, the complainant shall be informed that the grievance has been reviewed and of the relevant outcome or action taken.

chapters.title: Remediation Procedure
chapters.text:
The remediation procedure aims to provide comprehensive support for victims of grievances within the workplace, ensuring that any harm caused to the employee is properly addressed. While the company’s reputation is important, this procedure prioritizes the needs and well-being of the victim to help restore their dignity, fairness, and a safe working environment. The goal is not only to correct any wrongdoing but also to ensure that victims feel supported and that the harm caused is remedied in a meaningful and timely manner.
Grievances may arise from a wide range of issues within the workplace, and each type of grievance will require tailored remediation actions to address the specific harm caused to the victim. These grievances may include, but are not limited to:
- Working Conditions
- Health and Safety
- Employment Terms
- Child labor, Forced labor and Human trafficking
- Work Relationships
- Discrimination
- Harassment
- Job Role and Responsibilities
- Career management
- Company Policies and Procedures
- Disciplinary Action
- Performance Appraisals
- Discrimination and Equal Opportunity
- Compensation and Recognition
## Root Cause Analysis
After the grievance is resolved, a thorough analysis of the root cause of the issue must be conducted. This analysis serves as a critical tool to prevent future grievances and ensure that any systemic issues or gaps in existing policies and procedures are addressed. The root cause analysis involves a detailed review of the circumstances that led to the grievance, the decision-making process, and any existing policies, practices, or systems that may have contributed to the issue.
The Root Cause Analysis conducted by the Department Head with input from the Human Resources Department, relevant employees, and other stakeholders. This process will identify areas where improvements can be made to prevent similar grievances in the future, allowing the company to implement more effective preventative measures.
Once the root causes are identified, they will inform the remediation actions that are taken to resolve the grievance and address systemic issues. This leads directly into the next stages of the remediation procedure, ensuring that corrective actions are not only reactive but also proactive in addressing the broader work environment.
## Proportionality: Identification of Appropriate Responses
The remediation process should be proportional to the severity and nature of the grievance, ensuring that responses are fair, balanced, and considerate of the victim’s needs. After a grievance is raised, the company must first assess the impact of the issue on the victim, taking into account their emotional, psychological, and professional well-being. This process will involve the following actions:
- Consultation with Victims: The company actively engage with the victim during the assessment process to understand the full extent of their grievance. This includes consulting with the employee to gather their perspective on what actions they believe would address the harm caused. This consultation ensures that the response is tailored to the specific needs of the victim and that they feel heard and supported.
- Restorative Actions for the Victim: Depending on the nature of the grievance (discrimination, harassment, performance issues, etc.), the company should provide remedies that may include:
- Psychological Support: Offering counseling services through Employee Assistance Programs (EAPs) or external providers to address the emotional impact of grievances such as harassment or discrimination.
- Professional Support: Providing career coaching or mentoring to rebuild the victim’s confidence and restore their professional trajectory.
- Adjustment of Work Conditions: Modifying the work environment or responsibilities to ensure the victim's safety and comfort.
- Compensation for Losses: Offering financial compensation or career adjustments for any losses incurred due to the grievance.
- Appropriate Sanctions for Perpetrators: If misconduct is identified, appropriate actions must be taken. These may include disciplinary measures, corrective actions, and required training for the perpetrator, all proportionate to the severity of the violation.
## Specific Remediation for Child Labour, Forced Labour and Human Trafficking
Where child labour, forced labour or human trafficking is identified or reasonably suspected, the Company shall take prompt action to protect the affected individual from further harm.
The Company shall assess the immediate safety and well-being of the affected individual and determine appropriate remediation based on the nature and severity of the case.
Remediation may include, as appropriate:
- removal from the harmful situation;
- restoration of freedom of movement;
- return of personal identification documents;
- reimbursement of unlawful recruitment fees or deposits;
- payment of unlawfully withheld wages or benefits;
- medical support;
- psychological support;

chapters.title: Misconduct:
chapters.text:
- Company believes that employees and workmen must respect the discipline at work and errant employees / workmen must be dealt with stern actions. However, before any one holding as guilty of any charge, he must be given opportunity of hearing. No one will be condemned unheard. Principles of natural justice shall be respected in later and spirit.
Managing Director
- The following will amount to misconducts. The list is illustrative:
- Deliberate refusal to obey the lawful and reasonable instructions of the superior officer.
- Gross negligence of work
- Remaining absent from work without the permission of the leave sanctioning authority for three or more days.
- Intentionally damaging company’s property
- Using mobile phone or any other electronic devices within company premises without the permission of the competent authority
- Refusing to frisk checking at Security gate.
- Refusal to display identity cards
- Deliberate action to remove safety guards provided for safety of machine and employees / workmen.
- Collecting fund within the company premises with or receipts or without receipts but without the permission of Factory Manager.
- Riotous or disorderly or rude behaviour with co-workers / employees’ superior officers/ visitors of the company.
- Go-slow individual or in combination with others
- Instigating others to slow down or stop the work to cause disorderly, riotous behaviour, rude behaviour in the company premises
- Staging Demonstration or dharana or gherao within the company premises or in front of the company gates or within 200 meters of the company premises alone or under the aegis of any other organization.
- Stopping work individually or in concerted manner along with others
- Threatening co-workers, employees, workmen or officers, managers of the company within the company premises or outside the company premises on the issues having connection with the employment related issues.
- Stilling or attempting to still company’s or co-worker’s property.
- Smoking.
- Consuming alcohol while on duty or reporting for work under the influence of alcohol or any other intoxicating material.
- Tobacco Consumption in any form
- Gambling /Doing Personal Business / Playing Cards
- Collecting / Extorting money whether cash or in kind or through cheque or through any electronic media from co-workers, company’s contractors or vendors for any company worlers.
- Spitting
- Sexual Harassment as defined under the SHWWA.
Any other act of indiscipline
- Procedure:
- On occurrence of any such misconduct, workmen / employees covered within the definition of workman will dealt with following procedure
- Issue a Show Cause Notice,
- If reply to SCN is not satisfactory A charge sheet containing specific charges, list of witnesses and list of documents to be relied will be issued to workman / workmen.
- A domestic enquiry will be conducted as per principle of natural justice by a person appointed as Enquiry Officer. The case of company will be represented in the enquiry by a person appointed as Presenting Officer / Management Representative. Enquiry Officer should be well versed with the practice, procedure and principles of natural justice.
- Workman/ workmen will have right to keep a Defence Representative in the enquiry, who have to be from co-workers or can be an office bearer of the registered union to which delinquent workmen / workman are / is (a) member(s).
- After the enquiry, Enquiry Officer shall submit his report to the Appointing authority. Having considered the report, the Appointing authority will issue a Second Show Cause Notice to the delinquent employees giving him opportunity to make his say on the enquiry, findings and proposed penalty on delinquent workman / workmen.
- After considering the reply to second show cause notice, appointing authority will form his opinion whether to accept the enquiry proceedings, findings and what penalty to impose accordingly order will be issued.
- Delinquent workmen / workman can be placed under suspension during the enquiry if Disciplinary Authority forms an opinion that his presence will be detrimental to the law and order in the company, he may manipulate the documents vital to the enquiry or may influence the witnesses in the enquiry. However, during the suspension, he will be paid subsistence allowance @ 50% of gross wages. He will not be entitled for PF, bonus, leave during the period of suspension.
In case of non-workmen / non-workman, this procedure will be followed but strict documentation will not be necessary.
- The following penalties can be imposed:
- Warning / Censure
- Fine
- Stoppage of increments
- Demotion
- Punitive Suspension not exceeding four days
- Termination / dismissal
- The principles for determination of penalties are:
- Past Record of delinquent workmen / workman.
- Gravity of the misconduct.
- General impact upon other workmen of the company.

chapters.title: Separation
chapters.text:
If an employee wishes to leave the services of the Company after the completion of the Minimum Commitment Period (if applicable) given in the Appointment Letter/ Agreement at the time of joining, the employee will have to submit a resignation letter with a notice period as stipulated in the Appointment Letter/ Agreement.
The Resignation Letter will have to be handed over to the Department Head and a copy of the same forwarded to the Human Resources Department. Only after the concurrence of the CEO or General Manager is obtained, will the separation process be initiated. Once an employee resigns, he/she will not be covered under any ongoing review.
Upon separation from the company, the employee is required to return all property, equipment, materials, records and documents that have been borrowed from the company. The employee should also obtain clearance of all outstanding dues to/from the company.
## Acceptance of Resignation
The Reporting Manager can grant acceptance of a resignation. This is to be done after the Reporting Manager has had a meeting with the employee who wishes to resign. No commitments will be made orally to an employee who has resigned.
A note must accompany the letter of resignation from the Reporting Manager elaborating the reasons for the resignation and the date of relieving. Resignations are accepted taking into consideration the replacement plans for the position and planned for an effective handover.
All employees irrespective of rank are bound to give working notice as outlined in the Appointment Letter. Leave cannot be taken /granted when an associate is serving the notice period. The notice period for Trainee’s/Interns is 48 hours.
The notice period starts from the day the written resignation is accepted by the immediate Reporting Manager/ Regional Manager. For this reason, the Department Heads are requested to inform HR as soon as the first intimation is received.
## Waiving of Notice Period
In certain cases, the notice period agreement term can be waived. This decision can be taken by the Reporting Manager if and only if he obtains written endorsement from the Department Head / CEO with a copy to HR.
This decision is at the discretion of management. Comparisons/precedence’s may neither be quoted, nor will be entertained. In event employee has failed to complete the working notice period, the Company will view it very seriously and reserves the right to seek any legal measures.
## Clearance Procedure
A resignation acceptance / acknowledgement letter shall be sent to the employee from the Reporting Manager along with the necessary No Dues Certificate for obtaining clearance from relevant Departments.
The latest form can be received from HR (No Dues Firm). Obtaining the necessary clearances from all departments is the employee’s responsibility.
Employee should begin this procedure about 3 days in advance to his last date in the organization and send it to HR for generation of relieving documents.
If you are in possession of Company assets, (for example Cell phone/Laptop/Corporate Credit Card/ Data Cards) full & final settlement will be initiated only after you hand them back in perfect condition to the Company, along with the duly filled “No Dues Certificate”.
## Termination and Disciplinary Action
In the event when the management decides to terminate the services of an employee, the company will provide notice as per the Appointment Letter or equivalent notice salary to the employee based on his/her status (trainee, probationary, confirmed etc) with the company.
General Statement on Disciplinary Procedures
The Company reserves the right to discipline and/or terminate any employee who violates company policies, practices or rules of conduct. Poor performance and misconduct are also grounds for discipline / termination. To ensure uniformity and fairness in the treatment of everyone, certain disciplinary procedures have been established.
The following actions are unacceptable and considered grounds for disciplinary action. This list is not comprehensive; rather, it is meant merely as an example of the types of conduct that this company does not tolerate. The company reserves the right to determine the severity and extent of any disciplinary action based on the circumstances of each case. Actions that could result in disciplinary procedure include:
- Engaging in acts of discrimination or harassment in the workplace;
- Possessing, distributing or being under the influence of illicit controlled substances;
- Being under the influence of a controlled substance or alcohol at work, on company premises, or while engaged in company business;
- Unauthorized use of company property, equipment, devices or assets;
- Damage, destruction or theft of company property, equipment, devices or assets;
- Removing company property without prior authorization or disseminating company information without authorization;
- Falsification, misrepresentation or omission of information, documents or records;
…

chapters.title: Retirement
chapters.text:
Company believes that after a fulfilment of working age employees should leave peaceful evenings of their life. Therefore, they must retire at a particular point of their age very gracefully. The normal retirement age is 58 years. As per the requirements of the company, retirement age of any employee can be extended and the same needs to be accepted by the employee.
- The age of retirement in the company is 58 years.
- All retirements will take place on the last working day of the month in which the employee attains the age of 58 years.
- No advance notice will be required to retiring employee/workmen.
- Retiring employee will be given 15 days leave in the retiring month to make arrangements for life after retirement.
- On the last day of his working, he will produce no dues certificate from all department s of the company.
- The age for retirement shall be completed based on following documents;
- Birth certificate granted by Registrar of Deaths and Births.
- Matriculation certificate/mark sheet.
- School leaving certificate.
- Date of Birth of the employee/workmen will be enter in to the service record by the HR Dept. After verification of any of original documents listed at Para 6 above.
- Once a DOB is finalized it will not be changed/corrected. Driving license, PAN Card, Adhar Card, Voter’s Card, LIC Policy, or Bank Accounts will not be considered as a proof for DOB.

chapters.title: Code of Conduct
Conflict of Interest
chapters.text:
Each Employee is expected to avoid situations in which his or her financial or other personal interests or dealings are, or may be, in conflict with the interests of the Company. Accordingly, the Company expects its Employees to act in the Company's interest at all times.
Employees are advised not to engage in any other business, commercial or investment activity that may conflict with their ability to perform their duties to the Company. Employees must also not engage in any other activity (cultural, political, recreational, social) which could reasonably conflict with the Company's interests and interfere with the performance of their duties.
Employees must not use any Company's property, information or position, or opportunities arising from Code of Conduct & Workplace Ethics these for personal gains or to compete with or to tarnish the image of the Company.
Employees should not engage in any business activity, which could be detrimental to, or in competition with, the Company's any business activities.
All Employees must avoid situations in which their personal interest could conflict with the interest of the Company. If, under any circumstance, Employees' personal interests conflict with those of the Company's', in all such cases the Employee must seek advice from his or her reporting/ reviewing manager or from senior management.
For avoidance of doubt, mere financial portfolio investments shall not be considered as activities that conflict with the business of the Company.
## Confidentiality of Information
As a result of employment with the Company, Employees may be entrusted with confidential information; with regard to the Company and/or its affiliates, its customers and suppliers. The terms and conditions of of the confidentiality obligation and treatment of confidential information and intellectual property of the Company are mentioned in the “Appointment Letter”, which the Employees must read, acknowledge and sign.
## ntegrity of Financial Information
Shareholders, management and other interested parties must have complete and accurate financial information in order to make informed decisions. Many Employees participate in accounting processes that directly impact the integrity of external financial statements and internal management reports. All such Employees have a responsibility to ensure that all transactions are recorded in Company's accounts accurately and promptly and they must immediately report any known inaccuracies. Misrepresentations by Employees that result from intentional acts that may conceal or obscure the true nature of a business transaction are clear contraventions of this Policy.
## Protection and Use of Company Property
All Employees of the Company are responsible for protecting and taking reasonable steps to prevent the theft or misuse of, or damage to Company's assets, including all kinds of physical assets, movable, immovable and tangible property, corporate information and intellectual property such as inventions, copyrights, patents, trademarks and technology and intellectual property used in carrying out their responsibilities. All Employees must use all equipment s, tools, materials, supplies, and Employee time only for Company's legitimate business interests. Company's property must not be borrowed, loaned, or disposed of, except in accordance with appropriate Company's policies. All Employees must use and maintain Company's property and resources efficiently and with due care and diligence.
## Acceptance of Gifts and Other Benefits
Employees should not give or accept gifts, entertainment, or any other personal benefit or privilege that would in any way influence or appear to influence any business decision. Accepting money, gifts, entertainment, loans or any other benefit or preferential treatment from any existing or potential customer, supplier or business associate of the Company, is strictly prohibited, except occasional gifts of modest value and entertainment on a modest scale as part of customary business practice.
As a general principle, gifts of minor estimated value (e.g. pens, golf balls, desk diaries) are acceptable. Where the estimated value of the gift is considered to be over Rs. 2500, such gift should be declined.
All other prospective offers of gifts or entertainment falling outside the foregoing guideline, but which reflect customary and transparent business practice in a particular market, may be accepted. However, in case of doubts, the Employee must refer the case to his/her reporting manager and/or the relevant business unit head who will decide on the action to be taken.
It is unacceptable to directly or indirectly offer, pay, solicit or accept any kind of inducements or bribes. Any attempted transaction of this nature should be immediately reported to the Department Head or the HR Department. The funds and resources of the Company shall not be used directly or indirectly for any such purpose.

chapters.title: Harassment
chapters.text:
The Company is committed to provide a work environment that is free of inappropriate behaviour of all kinds and harassment on account of age, physical disability, marital status, race, religion, caste, sex, sexual orientation or gender identity. Employees are responsible for supporting the Company in its endeavour to protect others from any form of such harassments. In the course of business conduct of any Employee, wherever harassment occurs to any such Employee as a result of an act or omission by any third party or outsider, the Company shall take all steps necessary and reasonable to assist such affected Employee in terms of support and preventive action. This is separately detailed in the “Prevention of Workplace Harassment Policy”.
To further uphold this commitment, the Company has implemented a variety of measures, including:
- Regular awareness and sensitivity training on workplace conduct, diversity, inclusion, and harassment for all employees, including managers and senior leadership.
- A clearly defined and accessible reporting mechanism, allowing employees to report incidents confidentially and without fear of retaliation.
- Prompt and impartial investigation procedures led by trained internal committees to address complaints swiftly and fairly.
- A comprehensive Workplace Harassment Policy, which outlines prohibited behavior, complaint processes, and disciplinary consequences.
- Onboarding orientation modules to educate new employees about acceptable conduct and reporting procedures from the outset.
- Visible communication campaigns (posters, intranet messages, town halls) to reinforce the Company’s commitment to a harassment-free workplace.
- Manager accountability and training, ensuring that all leaders uphold and promote a respectful culture and intervene in early signs of inappropriate behavior.
- Support mechanisms such as counseling assistance, HR helplines, and confidential grievance redressal channels to assist affected employees.
Regular audits and culture surveys to monitor workplace climate and identify potential gaps in awareness or enforcement.
## Alcohol & Substance Abuse
The use or possession of alcohol, illegal drugs, and other controlled substances in the workplace and being under the influence of these substances on the job and during working hours is strictly prohibited. However, possession of prescription medication for medical treatment is permitted. There may be company-sponsored events where management approves the serving of alcoholic beverages. In these cases, all appropriate liquor laws must be followed, including laws regarding the prohibition of serving of Code of Conduct & Workplace Ethics alcohol to those under the legally permissible age. However, under all such cases, excessive drinking, intoxication and misbehavior at these events is prohibited and will be dealt with severely.
## Fraud
Fraud – or the act or intent to cheat, trick, steal, deceive, or lie – is both dishonest and, in most cases, criminal. Intentional acts of fraud are subject to strict disciplinary action, including dismissal and possible civil and/or criminal action against the concerned Employee. Some examples of Fraud include:
- Submitting false expense reports;
- Forging or altering checks;
- Misappropriating assets or misusing Company's property;
- Unauthorized handling or reporting of transactions;
- Inflating sales numbers by shipping inventory known to be defective or non-conforming;
- Making any entry on Company records or financial statements that is not accurate and in accordance with proper accounting standards
## Compliance with Laws and Agreements
All Employees shall conduct business in compliance with all applicable laws and regulations of the particular District, State or Country.
## Health, Safety and Environment
All Employees shall comply with the company health and safety norms as communicated to them from time to time. Employees shall bring to the management's attention any workplace safety or health hazard.
Misconduct and Non-Conformance With The Policy
Non-Observance of This Policy shall be construed as misconduct that could warrant disciplinary action, including dismissal in deserving cases. The decision in this regard will lie with the Management, including the Business Unit Head and concerned HR Manager and shall be binding on the Employees.
Exceptions
Any exceptions to the norms laid down in this Policy may be at the discretion of the CEO or any appropriate authority delegated by them.
Accountability
It is a condition of an appointment and/ or employment that all Employees must understand and adhere to the Company's Code of Conduct and at all times and abide by the standards, requirements and procedures laid down herein. They must:
- commit to individual conduct in accordance with this Policy.
- observe both, the spirit and the letter of the law in their dealings on Company's behalf.
